justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Memory and attention retraining show consistent gains in TBI/stroke populations. Generalization to daily function is moderate.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Multi-day seminar series; moderate cost; limited course locations; requires annual recertification.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable for OT/SLP in TBI, stroke, and acquired brain injury programs; limited outside cognitive rehab settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Cognitive rehab billed under OT/SLP codes; some commercial payers reference ACRM guidelines for authorization; no dedicated code.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate demand in inpatient rehab and TBI programs; not widely listed in general OT/SLP postings.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Engagement is high when goals are meaningful; fatigue is a limiting factor in early post-injury phases.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Concussion/TBI families and long-COVID brain fog patients will pay cash, but market is still developing.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: ACRM training carries weight in medico-legal and concussion clinic contexts where premium rates exist.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Genuinely rare among OTs/SLPs/PTs; meaningful differentiator.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Protocol-trainable but heavily clinician-judgment based; moderate leverage.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Patients ask for 'concussion specialist,' not ACRM-certified specifically.
justifications.business.efficiency: Multi-day training, meaningful cost; not cheap or fast.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: ACRM is a serious rehab research society; the credential is well-respected for neuro/cog faculty roles.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Strong association with active TBI/stroke researchers and Archives of PM&R.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Directly relevant to TBI/stroke/cognition content across OT/PT/SLP programs.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: INCOG and ACRM guidelines built on strong systematic review base.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Preferred for neuro/cog faculty lines, though not universally required.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Significant time and cost commitment relative to other geriatric/neuro adds.
